findings.title: Converter tests miss some remote shapes
findings.description: The `repoUrlFromRemote` case table in `tests/remote.test.ts` has no entry for `https://` userinfo without `.git`, `https://` with a port and no `.git`, or scp-like `user@host:owner/repo` without `.git`, so the accepted-form matrix is incomplete. The shared regexes would likely accept these shapes, but a regression in one branch would pass the suite unnoticed.

findings.title: A Windows drive path becomes a bogus web link
findings.description: The `SCP` pattern accepts any `host:owner/repo` with a host of letters, digits, dots and dashes, so a single-letter host such as `C:work/repo` matches. On Windows git treats that as a drive-relative local path, not an SSH remote, so `--origin` turns it into links to `https://C/work/repo` instead of rejecting it as the ticket's 'a local path is rejected' rule requires.

findings.title: Unlisted .git and userinfo stripping
findings.description: `repoUrlFromRemote` removes a `.git` suffix and userinfo from the remote before the result reaches checkRepoUrl(), but AGENTS.md rule 6 lists neither as documented framing, and the PR notes wrongly claim it does. Any later parser that strips them is treated as compliant, and no amendment with a test accompanies this change.

findings.title: Out-of-range SSH ports are accepted
findings.description: The SSH pattern accepts any digit run as the port, and the port is then discarded, so `ssh://git@host:0/o/r` and `ssh://git@host:99999/o/r` convert to a valid link. The HTTPS form rejects the same ports through checkRepoUrl(), so the two forms disagree on identical malformed values.

findings.title: Origin links can point to another repository
findings.description: `readOriginRemote()` runs Git with the caller's inherited environment, allowing `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_CONFIG_*` to change which origin it reads. When `render --origin` runs under a hook or wrapper that sets those variables, it can render links from a different repository instead of the one in the current directory.

findings.title: An untrusted checkout can run its own git on Windows
findings.description: `readOriginRemote` passes the bare name `'git'` to `execFileSync`. On Windows, Node resolves a bare program name by checking the current directory before `PATH`, so running `render --origin` inside a checkout that ships a `git.exe` at its root runs that file instead of the installed git. This is the first time tracenotes starts a process, and the tool is meant to be pointed at whatever repository the user is standing in, so a cloned third-party repository becomes a way to run code on the user's machine.

findings.title: Origin tests depend on user Git settings
findings.description: `isolatedGitEnv()` removes `GIT_*` variables but retains the caller's home-directory Git configuration. If that configuration defines `remote.origin.url`, the temporary repository created without an origin can acquire one and fail its expected error assertion.

review_agent_comment: The parser follows the ticket closely. As a follow-up, consider tightening host validation in `checkRepoUrl`, since `--origin` now passes remote hosts through it. The same behavior already exists for `--repo-url`.
